newsitem.title: USA: S&P says div increases fell in September.
newsitem.headline: S&P says div increases fell in September.

text.p: Standard & Poor's Corp said on Tuesday that September was the second consecutive month of year-to-year declines in the number of divided increases reported.
Standard & Poor's, a division of McGraw-Hill Cos, said this year's third quarter saw a 4.5 percent drop in dividend increases to 402 from 421 in the same period in 1995.
That was the first time the number of dividend hikes for a quarter registered a year-to-year decline since the first quarter of 1995, it said.
Standard & Poor's said that despite this year's third-quarter drop, the number of dividend increases for the nine months through September stood at 1,556, up 10.4 percent from 1995's 1,410.

"The slowdown in dividend increases may mean that companies are conserving cash out of fear that profits will level off in 1997," Arnold Kaufman, editor of The Outlook, Standard & Poor's weekly investment advisory newsletter, said in a statement.
"With the major stock market averages back to new highs, shareholders don't seem to be pressuring corporations to boost dividends," he added.
